newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT -Bunds hemmed in, must vault 103.48.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT -Bunds hemmed in, must vault 103.48.

text.p: September Bund futures on LIFFE will struggle to break out of a narrow 102.63 to 103.48 range on Wednesday as a lack of momentum leaves the contract floundering, technical analysts said.
"I don't see anything that will really push the market hugely out of those ranges for the short term," said Marc Ostwald, technical analyst at London Bond Broking.
"We must break above the 103.48/52 area to be able to make any progress toward testing that old high at 104.04," he added. "But momentum is appalling."
By 0655 GMT, September Bunds were up 0.08 at 103.18.
Charts show the market hit a high of 103.48 on July 24 and 103.52, the contract high, on July 23. The record high at 104.04 was touched on February 18.
Ostwald said to the downside, a band of congestion at 102.92/95 would lend some support to the market.
"If we get below there, we could go to some previous lows at 102.63/68," he added. The market dipped to 102.63 on July 25, and 102.68 on July 28.
But the summer lull and the uncertain market conditions mean investors will be reluctant to pile into the market, leaving it to drift sideways for the time being, analysts said.
Donna Liu, technical analyst at DKB International in London, put initial resistance at 103.35. "The downside in this market is still limited near-term," she told Reuters Financial Television.
Above 103.35, Liu said 103.50 was major resistance. "If the market cannot break through this level, it could see a setback," she said.
Analysts at HSBC Futures also said 103.50 would be tough resistance to crack. To the downside, they put solid support at 102.75 then 102.53, with a slightly weaker prop at 102.30.
By 0720 GMT, December Euromarks were down 0.01 at 96.55.
